arxiv-1810-03113.title: Control of uniflagellar soft robots at low Reynolds number using buckling instability
arxiv-1810-03113.creator: Mojtaba Forghani, Weicheng Huang, M. Khalid Jawed
arxiv-1810-03113.description: Abstract In this paper, we analyze the inverse dynamics and control of a bacteria-inspired uniflagellar robot in a fluid medium at low Reynolds number. Inspired by the mechanism behind the locomotion of flagellated bacteria, we consider a robot comprised of a flagellum—a flexible helical filament—connected to a spherical head.

arxiv-2008-05399.title: Improving information retrieval from electronic health records using dynamic and multi-collaborative filtering
arxiv-2008-05399.creator: Ziwei Fan
arxiv-2008-05399.description: Abstract Abstract Due to the rapid growth of information available about individual patients, most physicians suffer from information overload when they review patient information in health information technology systems. In this manuscript, we present a novel hybrid dynamic and multi-collaborative filtering method to improve information retrieval from electronic health records.

arxiv-2411-06547.creator: Roopendra Singh Rajawat \aff 1 \corresp, Tianhong Wang \aff 1, V. Khudik \aff 2 and Gennady Shvets \aff 1
arxiv-2411-06547.description: Abstract We present the process of ion acceleration using ultra-thin foils irradiated by elliptically polarized, high-intensity laser pulses. Recently, efficient generation of monoenergetic ion beams was introduced using the concept of laser-ion lensing and acceleration (LILA) ( Wang et al., 2021 ) .

arxiv-2503-09645.title: Global Position Aware Group Choreography using Large Language Model
arxiv-2503-09645.creator: Haozhou Pang, Tianwei Ding, Lanshan He, Qi GanSoul AI, China
arxiv-2503-09645.description: Abstract Dance serves as a profound and universal expression of human culture, conveying emotions and stories through movements synchronized with music. Although some current works have achieved satisfactory results in the task of single-person dance generation, the field of multi-person dance generation remains relatively novel.

arxiv-2507-04930.title: RainShift: A Benchmark for Precipitation Downscaling Across Geographies
arxiv-2507-04930.creator: Paula Harder, Luca Schmidt, Francis Pelletier, Nicole Ludwig, Matthew Chantry, Christian Lessig, Alex Hernandez-Garcia, David Rolnick
arxiv-2507-04930.description: Abstract Earth System Models (ESM) are our main tool for projecting the impacts of climate change. However, running these models at sufficient resolution for local-scale risk-assessments is not computationally feasible. Deep learning-based super-resolution models offer a promising solution to downscale ESM outputs to higher resolutions by learning from data.

arxiv-2510-12982.title: Galactic X-ray Transients in the First eROSITA All Sky Survey 2026 Galactic X-ray Transients in the First eROSITA All Sky Survey – 2
arxiv-2510-12982.creator: Vikash Maan, Aman Katira, Kunal. P. Mooley
arxiv-2510-12982.description: Abstract Although a multitude of studies have focused on targeted observations of Galactic X-ray transients, blind surveys and population studies have been limited. We have used the ROSAT , eROSITA and Gaia source catalogs to find Galactic X-ray transients having timescales < < 30 years.

pmc-11548574.title: A Cross-Attention-Based Class Alignment Network for Cross-Subject EEG Classification in a Heterogeneous Space
pmc-11548574.creator: Sufan Ma, Dongxiao Zhang
pmc-11548574.description: Background: Domain adaptation (DA) techniques have emerged as a pivotal strategy in addressing the challenges of cross-subject classification. However, traditional DA methods are inherently limited by the assumption of a homogeneous space, requiring that the source and target domains share identical feature dimensions and label sets, which is often impractical in real-world applications.

pmc-11628946.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) for paediatric fracture detection: a multireader multicase (MRMC) study protocol
pmc-11628946.creator: Susan C Shelmerdine, Cato Pauling, Emma Allan, Dean Langan, Emily Ashworth, Ka-Wai Yung, Joy Barber, Saira Haque, David Rosewarne, Nick Woznitza, Sarim Ather, Alex Novak, Kanthan Theivendran, Owen J Arthurs
pmc-11628946.description: IntroductionPaediatric fractures are common but can be easily missed on radiography leading to potentially serious implications including long-term pain, disability and missed opportunities for safeguarding in cases of inflicted injury. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist fracture detection in adult patients exist, although their efficacy in children is less well known.

pmc-12391700.title: Self-assembled hybrid hydrogel microspheres create a bone marrow-mimicking niche for bone regeneration
pmc-12391700.creator: Zhi He, Peilun Hu, Zifan Li, Kaige Mao, Jingchuan Zheng, Chun-Yi Yang, Yuyang Luo, Jia Yang, Zheng Cao, Jingsong Lu, Xiaobin Luo, Sengpav Tong, Zhijun He, Kunkoo Kim, Yaosai Liu, Xiaodan Sun, Lingyun Zhao, Yongwei Pan, Yongping Cao, Yu Wang, Xiumei Wang
pmc-12391700.description: Bone marrow (BM), a natural niche rich in growth factors and bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), provides an optimal regenerative microenvironment and is widely used in clinical applications. However, the limited proliferative capacity of BMSCs and the mismatch between bone regeneration and growth factors release constrain their effectiveness in treating critical bone defects.

pmc-12422516.title: YOLOv11-WBD: A wavelet-bidirectional network with dilated perception for robust metal surface defect detection
pmc-12422516.creator: Li Guan, Haitao Zhang, Yijun Zhou, Xinyu Du, Mingxuan Li
pmc-12422516.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In the field of quality control, metal surface defect detection is an important yet challenging task. Although YOLO models perform well in most object detection scenarios, metal surface images under operational conditions often exhibit coexisting high-frequency noise components and spectral aliasing background textures, and defect targets typically exhibit characteristics such as small scale, weak contrast, and multi-class coexistence, posing challenges for automatic defect detection systems.

pmc-12557533.title: Broadband topological transitions in twisted elastodynamic metasurfaces
pmc-12557533.creator: Simon Yves, Yu-Gui Peng, Andrea Alù
pmc-12557533.description: SignificanceWe extend the concept of twistronics to elastodynamic metasurfaces with broken symmetries, unlocking exquisite control over phonon fields. Notably, we predict and experimentally demonstrate broadband, reconfigurable, and robust topological transitions for flexural waves, modifying their dispersion topology from elliptic to hyperbolic by twisting a pair of identical elastic metasurfaces.

pmc-12733443.title: Special Issue: Emerging Topics in Metal Complexes: Pharmacological Activity, 2nd Edition
pmc-12733443.creator: Agnieszka Ścibior, Manuel Aureliano, Juan Llopis
pmc-12733443.description: num (Pt), zinc (Zn), vanadium (V), copper (Cu), magnesium (Mg), and other metal complexes and their mechanisms in treating Alzheimer’s disease (AD)), and the efficacy of platinum (Pt)-based complexes in the treatment of lung cancer. It also includes research into a promising radiotheranostic agent against prostate cancer and a novel Fe(III)-pyridoxal-derivative complex with serum proteins and DNA binding activities.

pmc-12887203.title: Metabolic Vulnerability Index and Atherosclerosis Incident: A Prospective Cohort Study From the UK Biobank
pmc-12887203.creator: Xiangliang Liu, Xinqiao Chen, Wang Yang, Yuwei He, Yuting Liu, Yuguang Li, Naifei Chen, Jiuwei Cui
pmc-12887203.description: BackgroundAtherosclerosis underlies most cardiovascular disease, but traditional factors incompletely explain risk. This study examined whether a novel Metabolic Vulnerability Index (MVX), integrating inflammatory and metabolic biomarkers, predicts incident atherosclerosis independently of traditional and genetic risks.MethodsWe analyzed data from 171 600 participants in the UK Biobank without baseline atherosclerotic disease (median follow‐up, 13.6 years).

pmc-13499186.title: Clavicle length and scapulothoracic angle in young children with internal rotation contracture secondary to brachial plexus birth palsy: a bilateral MRI study
pmc-13499186.creator: Jourdan H Meltzer, Michael L Pearl
pmc-13499186.description: BackgroundThe most common sequela of brachial plexus birth palsy (BPBP) is an internal rotation contracture (IRC) of the shoulder. The contracture is known to result primarily from restricted motion and deformity at the glenohumeral joint, and, to a lesser extent, decreased humeral retroversion (HRV).

pmc-13583278.title: How to Build Health Practitioners Research Capacity: An Umbrella Review
pmc-13583278.creator: Victoria Headlam, Jacqueline Penney, Ha Hoang, Elaine Hart, Sarah Prior, Marie-Louise Bird, Suzanne Waddingham
pmc-13583278.description: BackgroundBuilding research capacity, culture and capability (RCCC) among healthcare practitioners is essential for evidence-informed care. No umbrella review has synthesised review-level evidence on RCCC across professions and settings.ObjectiveTo synthesise and critically appraise systematic reviews on documented factors influencing RCCC among healthcare practitioners, and to identify strategies that strengthen these factors within healthcare settings.

uslaw-usc-t38-s7287.title: 38 U.S.C. § 7287 — Administration
uslaw-usc-t38-s7287.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t38-s7287.description: United States Code, Title 38 (Veterans’ Benefits); Part V (Boards, Administrations, And Services); Chapter 72 (United States Court Of Appeals For Veterans Claims); Subchapter III (Miscellaneous Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims may exercise, for purposes of management, administration, and expenditure of funds of the Court, the authorities provided.
